newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian state planning to sell duty-free shops.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian state planning to sell duty-free shops.

text.p: An Egyptian state holding company said on Friday it planned to sell some of its shares in Egypt Free Shops, one of its wholly owned subsidiaries.

The holding company, Housing, Tourism and Cinema Company, did not say how many shares or whether it would offer them to public subscription or to strategic investors. It said it would give more details soon.

Egypt Free Shops, which has a monopoly on duty-free shops in Egypt, made profits for distribution of 13.423 million pounds ($3.95 million) in the financial year 1995/6, which ended on June 30. It forecast the 1996/7 figure would be 15 million.

The company has a paid-in capital of 35 million pounds, divided into 3.5 million shares with a nominal value of 10 pounds each. It forecast that at the end of 1996/7 reserves and deferred profits would amount to 31.891 million pounds, giving total shareholders' funds a value of 66.891 million.
The agent for the sale of the shares will be National Bank of Egypt, the holding company said.
In 1994 the holding company offered Egypt Free Shops as a complete unit to a single investor. It said it received more than 10 offers but none of them ended in a deal.
